Write text as UTF-8, falling back to ASCII where it is not UTF-8

Source: R/txt.R
wrtxtfb.Rd

Writes text to path as UTF-8, one element per line, for generated text files (a README, a citation, a script) whose content may hold names with accents. An element that is not valid UTF-8 is written as its ASCII transliteration (asciifb()), so the file is always valid UTF-8.

Usage

wrtxtfb(text, path)

Arguments

text

The lines; as.character() converts any other type.

path

The file, one non-empty string; its directory must exist. A name with no suffix is given .txt.

Value

The path written, invisibly.

Details

The lines are joined with "\n", a final newline is added, and the bytes are written through a binary connection, so the file is UTF-8 whatever the session locale and its line endings are "\n" on every platform. An existing file is overwritten. A missing element is written as the two letters NA, and an empty text writes a file holding a single newline. A path that is not one non-empty string is refused before anything is written; a directory that does not exist is an error of the write.

See also

toascii().

Examples

p <- wrtxtfb(c("line one", "line two"), tempfile(fileext = ".txt"))
readLines(p)
#> [1] "line one" "line two"
q <- wrtxtfb("Author: \u00c1ngela Zorro Medina", tempfile())
readBin(q, "raw", 20)
#>  [1] 41 75 74 68 6f 72 3a 20 c3 81 6e 67 65 6c 61 20 5a 6f 72 72
try(wrtxtfb("x", c("a.txt", "b.txt")))
#> Error : wrtxtfb: `path` must be one non-empty file path.
